doc_locations.cited: p10 §12.4 '3.2.1 and 3.3.2, which allow sensitive authentication data to be retained ... until the transaction is settled.'
p10 §12.4 'incremental authorizations (ride-hailing tips, hotel extensions)'

findings.note: The risk is real, but the review leaves it unresolved when the answer can be checked. PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.3.1 and 3.3.1.2 forbid keeping the card verification code after authorization, even encrypted, and 3.3.2 covers only SAD stored before authorization completes. The design's reading is therefore wrong by definite knowledge, and keeping the CVC until settlement or for incremental authorizations breaks the confirmed AD-009. Saying 'cannot confirm or refute' is calibrated, but this is a missed research opportunity.

findings.note: This is a sound internal contradiction. The design's own text (p16 §20.2) makes zero RPO on regional loss unattainable. The payment table in §19 has no idempotency_key or request_hash column; it has merchant_account_id rather than merchant_id. Challenging AD-004 is justified by the design's own evidence. findings.note: The arithmetic is correct. The ACQ-TH1 file arrives at 06:30 ICT, which is 07:30 SGT (p12 §16.1). Adding 45 + 15 minutes (p13 §16.2) gives 08:30 SGT, after the 08:00 SGT deadline, and volume roughly doubles by 2027. Challenging AD-016 is justified by the design's own figures. The options offered (incremental matching, a cut-off, renegotiating the delivery time, or relaxing the SLA) are well bounded. Evidence location labels (EV-023 'p13/s3') are slightly wrong.

findings.note: The scale-out trigger can never fire: 55% card share of 2,000 TPS is 1,100 TPS, below the 1,500 TPS trigger. doc_locations.cited: p17 §21.1 'fewer than 1% of card payments cascade'
p20 §26.2 NFR-2 '3.8% retryable-outcome injection'

findings.note: Correct. The '<1%' premise contradicts the 3.8% baseline and the NFR-2 test. Because the 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds the 1,500 ms target, NFR-2 is likely to fail its own acceptance test. The review rates this medium, which understates it; it affects whether a requirement is achievable. The 3DS omission is a good extra observation. Shortening the timeout touches the confirmed cascade policy, and the finding acknowledges this as a refinement.

doc_locations.cited: p8 §9.3 'single partition sustains up to 10,000 write capacity units per second.'
p8 §9.3 'about 1,800 WCU at peak'

findings.note: The suspicion is right, but it is left unresearched. AWS documentation gives 1,000 WCU per partition, not 10,000. Writes are charged per 1 KB, so a 4 KB update costs at least 4 WCU plus LSI writes, and an LSI caps each partition-key item collection at 10 GB. So §9.3 is wrong by definite knowledge, and the largest merchant would be throttled. The review names the right levers (sharding, GSI, fail closed), but it calls the claim 'unverified' when it could easily have been checked. This is a missed research opportunity.
